transcript.text: fridge part freezin stuff, lettuce + yoghurts frozen solid at the back. hotpoint ff. any ideas pls

Even if the thermostat is set correctly, items pressed there will freeze solid while the rest of the fridge stays fine. 1. Move any lettuce, yoghurts or other items away from the back wall and vents so there is at least a few centimetres of space for air to circulate.
2. Ensure the temperature dial isn't set to its coldest setting (usually marked 'Max' or '7') unless you need it temporarily. If moving the food fixes it, that was just overcrowding against the cold source. If the items are still freezing after a day with plenty of space and normal settings, we'll need to look at whether ice has built up inside blocking airflow.
ok just checked, dial was on max, kids prob moved it. and the back is rammed after big shop, stuff pressed on the vent slots. will turn it down and clear it

That sounds like exactly what was happening: the dial on 'Max' combined with food blocking the vents would easily freeze items solid against the back wall. Turn the dial down to a mid-range setting (usually around 3 or 4) and leave at least a few centimetres of space between your food and the rear panel so air can circulate freely. Leave it for about 24 hours with the doors shut to let the temperature stabilise. If they are still freezing solid despite the correct setting and clear airflow, we'll need to look at whether ice has built up inside blocking the air from reaching the fridge compartment properly.
